title: Expectation splits over the last coordinate
statement:
Let $\varphi : \{0,1\}^{n+1} \to \bbr$ be a Boolean function on $n+1$ variables, and for a bit $b \in \{0,1\}$ let $\varphi_b : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$, $\varphi_b(x) = \varphi(x, b)$, be its restriction obtained by fixing the last coordinate to $b$. Then the expectation of $\varphi$ under the uniform measure on $\{0,1\}^{n+1}$ is the average of the expectations of its two restrictions:
\[
  \E[\varphi] \;=\; \frac{\E[\varphi_{0}] + \E[\varphi_{1}]}{2}.
\]
hypotheses_covered: φ is a Boolean function on n+1 variables
replaced:
The expectation of $\varphi$ on the cube of dimension $n+1$ is the average of the expectations
of its two restrictions:
\[
\E[\varphi] = \tfrac12\bigl(\E[\mathrm{restrictLast}\,\varphi\,\mathrm{false}] + \E[\mathrm{restrictLast}\,\varphi\,\mathrm{true}]\bigr).
\]
